source.layout: Call of Duty Wiki map pages (all 14 checked), plus callofdutymaps.com for named structures.
source.tactics: Where a map has a ZigZack IGN map-recon walkthrough, the callouts and positions come from that. Otherwise from BO1-era community guides where they exist, and reasoned from the layout where they don't. Each map's 'Checked against the wiki' list says which.
source.confidence: Each map lists what was verified against the wiki under 'Checked against the wiki'. Anything not listed there is inference.

maps.name: Nuketown
maps.identity: Two suburban houses facing each other across a road, with a bus and a truck in between. Nearly symmetrical, one of the smallest maps in the series, and the centre is a warzone you should mostly stay out of.

sides.name: House A
sides.spawn: The back garden behind your house. Don't linger — the gardens turn into killing fields the moment the match starts.
sides.opening: Three ways out: the road down either side of the house, straight through the ground floor, or upstairs. Either rush the opening by the truck in the middle, or take the upper floor. Both are real plans; crossing the open centre is not.
sides.flank: Down the side path past the garage, using the truck for cover.
sides.pinch: The side path by the flowers. It's one of the map's four chokepoints and it's watched from their front garden.

sides.name: House B
sides.spawn: The back garden behind the opposite house. Same warning — move out of it.
sides.opening: Either guard the front garage area to break their rush before it starts, or get to the second floor and hold the window over the centre.
sides.flank: The opposite side path, into their blind side.
sides.pinch: The front door approach. Covered from the upper floor opposite.

powerPositions.name: The upper floor of your own house
powerPositions.why: Elevation over the centre and the other house. Claymore both doorways behind you and you can watch the middle without being in it.

powerPositions.name: The opening by the truck in the centre
powerPositions.why: From here you cover three of the map's four chokepoints at once — the garage, the side path by the garage, and the front door. It's the strongest single spot on the map and most players never take it.

enemySpots.name: Both upper floors
enemySpots.note: Assume one is occupied at all times. The window over the centre is too good to leave empty.

enemySpots.name: Lying in the front-garden grass
enemySpots.note: A known ambush: prone in the grass by the garage, waiting for anyone taking the side path.

enemySpots.name: The garages
enemySpots.note: Each house has one and it covers the side approach — one of the four chokepoints.

maps.trap: Pushing past the bus and the truck. The moment your team is through the middle, the game has nowhere safe left on their end and starts spawning them behind your lines — so the kills you just got become shots in your back. On Nuketown the discipline is to hold your side of the vehicles, not to win the centre.

loadout.weaponWhy: 3-shot kill to 19.5m covers the whole map, and a 0.2s aim-in wins the corner fights.
loadout.perkWhy: The map is small enough that explosives are used liberally by everyone, and the two spawns are close enough for an opening grenade to reach.

deeper: Do not use the cars as cover — they explode when damaged, and the person shooting them knows that.
At the start of the match, a short pause and then a grenade lobbed over the house can catch the enemy still leaving their garden. Expect one coming the other way.

The spawn tell: if you're upstairs and see a teammate running from the opposite house, or an enemy appears from beneath you, the spawns have already flipped — turn round and cover the balcony behind you.
Attack helicopters are strong here because there's very little cover from above.
Concussion grenades decide more fights here than guns do. Tactical Mask Pro is a genuine counter.
verified: Two houses, two floors each, with a garage — map is nearly symmetrical (wiki)
Both teams spawn in a back garden area; three routes out: side road, ground floor, or upper floor (wiki)
The centre holds a bus and a truck; sightlines there favour SMGs and ARs (wiki)
The centre is a high-risk warzone best avoided; the two houses are the contested strongholds (community guide)
The opening by the truck controls three of the four chokepoints: garage, side path by the garage, and front door (2011 map guide)
Pushing past the bus causes enemies to respawn behind your lines (2011 map guide)
Cars explode when damaged and should not be used as cover (community guide)
Backyard spawn zones become killing fields immediately after the match starts (community guide)

maps.name: Firing Range
maps.identity: A compact training facility with three routes through it — left flank, middle road, right flank. Two elevated holds, the garage and top wooden, decide most games between them.

sides.name: OP 40 (south)
sides.spawn: The southern end of the map. The garage is directly in front of you.
sides.opening: Take the garage. It's elevated, it watches enemies crossing below, and it's one of the most popular spots on the map — so it's a race. From there you have access to the nook, below the sniper perch.
sides.flank: Garage into the sandbags, then transition into double barrels to watch the left flank with cover. An assault rifle covers that crossing well.
sides.pinch: The shipping container on the way out of the shooting range. Throw a flash or stun over it before you commit.

sides.name: Tropas (north)
sides.spawn: The northern end, by the second shooting range.
sides.opening: Contest top wooden. Controlling it gives your team eyes on most of the map, including top garage — and it has an escape into back alley if it turns.
sides.flank: Out through back alley, or down the side into the sandbags to peek top garage and lower mid.
sides.pinch: Moving through the shooting range itself. It's full of campers and spawn points — be thorough, don't sprint it.

powerPositions.name: Top wooden (the wooden bunker)
powerPositions.why: Eyes on most of the map, including top garage, and a clean escape into back alley. The single most valuable hold here.

powerPositions.name: The garage
powerPositions.why: Elevated over the crossings and one of the most popular spots on the map. Watches enemies moving below and connects to the nook.

enemySpots.name: Top garage
enemySpots.note: Named as a popular spot. Check it from wooden before you cross.

enemySpots.name: The sniper perch and the elevated middle structures
enemySpots.note: The map's sniping positions. Vulnerable to a lobbed grenade and to a knife in the back — which is also how you deal with them.

enemySpots.name: The second shooting range, down back alley
enemySpots.note: Home to many campers and to spawn points.

maps.trap: Moving without checking around you. The map is small and laid out so that the middle road and the crossings are covered from the garage, top wooden and the perch at once — run it blind and you're caught in a crossfire within seconds of spawning. Lower mid in particular is ground that gets peeked from above.

loadout.weaponWhy: 3-shot kill to 39.4m covers every sightline here, and an assault rifle is what you want for watching the left flank from the sandbags.
loadout.perkWhy: Spy Planes go up constantly on a map this small, and the flanks only work if they can't see you take them.

deeper: If someone is in the tower, don't duel them — lob a grenade or two up. It's small and enclosed, and that's the intended answer.
If you take an elevated spot, claymore the way up behind you, and don't stay scoped — the standard punishment here is a knife in the back.
Attack helicopters do well because the map offers very little aerial protection.
Snipers struggle: the map is too small for the ranges they need.
Gas into a contested area creates enough confusion to take it.
If you're running a suppressor, the FAMAS drops to a 3-shot kill inside 14m — across the middle that's a 4-shot kill.
verified: Tropas spawn is the northern end of the map; OP 40 spawn is the south (ZigZack, IGN map recon)
Three major routes: right flank, middle road, left flank (ZigZack)
The garage sits in front of the OP 40 spawn, is elevated, watches enemies crossing below, and is one of the most popular spots (ZigZack)
The nook sits below the sniper perch and is accessed from the garage (ZigZack)
Sandbags give cover and peek both sides; you can watch the left flank from them and transition into double barrels (ZigZack)
Controlling top wooden gives eyes on most of the map including top garage; sandbags peek top garage or lower mid; wooden escapes to back alley (ZigZack)
Back alley leads to a second shooting range, home to many campers and spawn points (ZigZack)
A choke point sits at the shipping container when exiting the shooting range — flash or stun the spawns beyond it (ZigZack)
Two elevated middle structures are the sniping spots; vulnerable to lobbed grenades and knifing, so claymore your back (Dominate Black Ops)
A bathroom hut in the north-west has two exits with sightlines to critical points (Dominate Black Ops)
Grenades lob into the high central tower reliably (Dominate Black Ops)
Little aerial protection, so helicopter streaks are strong (Dominate Black Ops)
Favours SMGs, ARs and LMGs; shotguns for defending; snipers difficult (CoD Wiki)

maps.name: Summit
maps.identity: A small mountain facility built around a central control room. Four major choke points, and every one of them involves that room — so the game is really about who owns the middle and whether you keep the enemy pushed back.

sides.name: Spetsnaz spawn
sides.spawn: The Spetsnaz side. Check every corner for campers before you move — it's a known problem here.
sides.opening: Push into the control room. On a map this small you have to keep pushing the enemy back, because that's what gives you favourable spawns.
sides.flank: Around or through the electrical room is a quick route to the porch, and a good peek onto people pushing.
sides.pinch: The electrical room route into the porch. It works, but it is a magnet for grenades.

sides.name: Black Ops spawn
sides.spawn: The Black Ops side.
sides.opening: Use the balcony first — it gives a clear view of some major spawn points, which tells you where they are before you commit to anything.
sides.flank: The rock area gives a long-range view down the west side; the skinny bridge from there leads to the back of the Spetsnaz spawn.
sides.pinch: The skinny bridge. Narrow, and good snipers pick players off through the trees around it.

powerPositions.name: Top control room
powerPositions.why: A hot spot and one of the bigger rooms on the map once all the glass is broken. Multiple levels, multiple windows, and about half a dozen entrances to watch.

powerPositions.name: The back area and the back stairs
powerPositions.why: Both named as underused. The back area gives great vision of nearby spawn points; the back stairs punish people who sprint up rather than holding.

enemySpots.name: Bottom control room
enemySpots.note: Where SMG players cruise — a variety of peeks and a lot of traffic.

enemySpots.name: The rock area
enemySpots.note: The sniper route. Any good sniper plays it for the long view down the west side.

enemySpots.name: Corners of the Spetsnaz spawn, and the porch
enemySpots.note: Campers sit in the spawn corners; the porch has good peeks and attracts thrown equipment.

maps.trap: Back rooms. It's one of the four choke points and it should be avoided — but it's also the quickest route to the porch, which is exactly why people keep taking it and keep dying in it. The porch itself then attracts thrown equipment, so the fast route punishes you twice.

loadout.weaponWhy: The control room is a bottom-and-top SMG fight with short peeks — 3-shot kill to 19.5m and a 0.2s aim-in suits it.
loadout.perkWhy: Half a dozen entrances to one room means people arrive from everywhere. Footsteps are the only warning you get.

deeper: A Motion Sensor in the right corner of the control room covers four popular choke spots at once — the highest-value piece of equipment on this map.
Toss a flash into middle hall; it very reliably catches people.
Breaking the glass in top control room changes the room — it becomes one of the biggest spaces on the map, with far more angles than people expect.
Double barrels gives a view of the Spetsnaz spawn buildings.
Constant pressure matters more here than on bigger maps: pushing the enemy back is what keeps your spawns favourable.
Lethal grenades and gas into the upper room of the compound shake people out of it.
verified: One of the smaller maps, with four major choke points, each involving the control room (ZigZack, IGN map recon)
On a map this size you must keep pushing the enemy to hold favourable spawns (ZigZack)

Top control room is a hot spot and one of the bigger rooms once the glass is broken (ZigZack)
A flash into middle hall reliably catches players (ZigZack)
The back area is underused and watches nearby spawn points; the back stairs are underrated (ZigZack)
The Black Ops spawn balcony gives a clear view of major spawn points (ZigZack)
The rock area is the sniper route, with a long view down the west side; double barrels views the Spetsnaz spawn buildings (ZigZack)
A skinny bridge leads to the back of the Spetsnaz spawn; snipers shoot through the trees there (ZigZack)
Around or through the electrical room is a quick route to the porch, and a grenade magnet (ZigZack)
The centre compound is where most kills occur; grenades and gas into the upper room work (Dominate Black Ops)
Set in the Ural Mountains with severe drops on all sides (CoD Wiki)

maps.name: Radiation
maps.identity: A uranium processing facility built around a central bunker, with tunnels running out to both sides and a set of steel blast doors over the middle that either team can open or close.

sides.name: Conveyor end
sides.spawn: The end with the conveyor belt — mind the crusher, it will kill you.
sides.opening: Head for the central bunker and use the tunnels rather than the open ground above them.
sides.flank: Through the tunnel network to the far side, coming up behind their line.
sides.pinch: The tunnel mouths. They're the obvious exits and they're covered from above.

sides.name: Factory end
sides.spawn: The factory end, near the explosive tanks and the control room.
sides.opening: Into the bunker through the near tunnel and hold a junction. The tunnels are the map's safe movement.
sides.flank: The outer route past the giant tanks toward their end.
sides.pinch: The walkway between the two giant tanks. Narrow, elevated, exposed.

powerPositions.name: The central bunker
powerPositions.why: It connects to both sides by tunnel, so holding it means controlling how the enemy can move rather than just where they can be shot.

powerPositions.name: A tunnel junction
powerPositions.why: Enclosed, short sightlines, and you hear people coming. The safest ground on the map.

enemySpots.name: Inside the central bunker
enemySpots.note: Contested constantly. Whoever is already still wins the doorway.

enemySpots.name: The tunnel exits
enemySpots.note: People wait at the mouths rather than inside them.

enemySpots.name: The control room and the walkway between the tanks
enemySpots.note: Both hold blast door switches, so both attract traffic.

maps.trap: Charging into the bunker through a doorway. Interiors reward whoever is already standing still with their gun up, and that is never the person who just sprinted in. Take the middle through a tunnel or don't take it.

loadout.weaponWhy: 3-shot kill to 45.7m with good handling — flexible enough for tunnel fights and the open ground above.
loadout.perkWhy: The tunnels only work as a flank if you aren't broadcasting yourself on their minimap.

deeper: The blast doors over the middle are controlled by two switches — one on a walkway between two giant tanks, one in the control room by the explosive tanks. Either switch opens or closes them, so the state of the middle can change without warning.
The conveyor belt near one spawn feeds a crusher that kills instantly. Know which end you're on.
Napalm on a tunnel mouth denies the map's safest route for a long time.
verified: Set in a uranium processing facility
Central bunker with tunnels leading directly out to both side areas
Steel blast doors over the middle, opened or closed by either of two switches
One switch sits on a walkway between two giant tanks, the other in a control room by the explosive tanks
A conveyor belt near one spawn leads into a crusher that kills the player

maps.name: Jungle
maps.identity: A ruined village and a small military base, split by a river. Officially a large map, heavy on verticality, with slopes and ladders linking levels and cover everywhere.

sides.name: Village end
sides.spawn: The ruined village side of the river.
sides.opening: The village is where most of the close-quarters fighting happens. Move through the huts and rocks rather than the open lanes between them.
sides.flank: Across the river toward the base, using the slopes and cover rather than the direct crossing.
sides.pinch: The river crossing. It's the seam between the two halves and both sides watch it.

sides.name: Base end
sides.spawn: The small military base side.
sides.opening: Use the ladders and slopes to get a level up before you push toward the village.
sides.flank: Round the edge of the base and across toward the village's far side.
sides.pinch: Coming out of the base into the open ground before the river. Exposed perches on the far side cover it.

powerPositions.name: One of the exposed perches
powerPositions.why: The map has a few of them with long lines of sight — the only spots where range beats concealment here.

powerPositions.name: Elevated in the village, behind cover
powerPositions.why: The village is the busiest part of the map. Height plus rocks and huts means you see the traffic without joining it.

enemySpots.name: The perches with long sightlines
enemySpots.note: The map supports sniping from a handful of specific spots. Learn them and check them.

enemySpots.name: Inside the village huts
enemySpots.note: Where most close-quarters fights happen. Dark and enclosed.

enemySpots.name: Behind rocks and trees
enemySpots.note: There's cover everywhere, which cuts both ways.

maps.trap: Playing it like a small map because the foliage makes it feel enclosed. It's officially a large map with ranged sightlines from the perches, so an SMG-and-sprint approach gets punished from distances you can't see. The vertical routes are safer than the direct ones.

loadout.weaponWhy: 3-shot kill to 45.7m and high damage for a map that mixes long perch sightlines with close village fights. Run a Grip.
loadout.perkWhy: Cover is everywhere and visibility is poor, so sound is the primary sensor in both directions.

deeper: The map encourages vertical movement — many slopes and ladders let you change level quickly. Use them; the ground routes are the watched ones.
The rice paddies to the north-east are an open level boundary that kills you with a landmine. Don't flank that way.
Foliage blocks your view, not bullets. If you see a muzzle flash in a bush, shoot the bush.
verified: Classified as a large map by Treyarch
Consists of a ruined village and a small military base, split by a river
Encourages vertical combat via many slopes and ladders
The village is well-trafficked and hosts most close-quarters fights
A few exposed perches offer long lines of sight for sniping
The north-eastern rice paddies are a level boundary that kills with a landmine

maps.name: Hanoi
maps.identity: A North Vietnamese prison with a barricaded street running along the outside. Set at night and genuinely dark — two different games depending on whether you're inside or out.

sides.name: Street end
sides.spawn: Toward the barricaded street side.
sides.opening: Go inside. The street is long and exposed, and there's nothing on it worth the risk in the opening seconds.
sides.flank: Through the prison interior and out at the far end of the street.
sides.pinch: Any doorway from the prison onto the street. Predictable exits, covered from the far end.

sides.name: Prison end
sides.spawn: The prison side.
sides.opening: Hold your half of the interior and let them come through the corridors — you know the rooms, they don't.
sides.flank: Along the barricaded street toward their side, using the barricades as cover.
sides.pinch: Where the street meets the prison. Open for a moment, and that's enough.

powerPositions.name: An interior position overlooking the street
powerPositions.why: You get the street's sightline with walls around you and exits behind you.

powerPositions.name: A prison corridor junction
powerPositions.why: Short angles suit whoever is already set, and the darkness works in favour of the person not moving.

enemySpots.name: The far end of the street
enemySpots.note: The longest sightline on the map. Someone is watching it.

enemySpots.name: Prison room corners
enemySpots.note: The rooms are small enough that whoever is already inside wins.

enemySpots.name: Behind the street barricades
enemySpots.note: Cover along the exposed lane, favouring the defender.

maps.trap: The barricaded street. It looks like the fast route between the ends and it's the most reliably fatal ground on the map. The interior gets you to the same place with walls in between.

loadout.weaponWhy: 3-shot kill to 21m and a fast aim-in for the interior fights, which is where the map should be played.
loadout.perkWhy: Thin prison walls and a lot of prefire. Penetration plus reduced flinch wins the close trades.

deeper: The night sky makes Spy Planes and Counter-Spy Planes very hard to see, so they get shot down far less often here. Your 3-kill streak is worth more on Hanoi than almost anywhere, and so is theirs.
The darkness rewards stillness. Moving players are far easier to pick out than stationary ones on this map.
There are two hidden RC-XD tunnels on this map if you run one.
verified: A North Vietnamese Army prison based on the Hanoi Hilton
Medium-sized, with a prison interior and a barricaded street along the outside
Set at night; the map is quite dark
The dark sky makes Spy Planes and Counter-Spy Planes hard to spot and shoot down
Two secret RC-XD tunnels

maps.name: Havana
maps.identity: A Cuban street scene shaped like Crossfire from CoD4 — one long main street with buildings down both sides and a lot of chokepoints. The street is the trap and the buildings are the game.

sides.name: West end
sides.spawn: The western end of the street.
sides.opening: Into the buildings first. Don't touch the street until you know where their long-range player is sitting.
sides.flank: Through the interiors and out behind their side.
sides.pinch: Every alley mouth onto the main street. One metre of open road, seen from the whole length of it.

sides.name: East end
sides.spawn: The eastern end of the street.
sides.opening: Take a building and hold a window onto the street — you get the sightline without standing in it.
sides.flank: Along the back routes parallel to the street.
sides.pinch: The exits from the buildings into the open. Overlooked from windows on both sides.

powerPositions.name: A window overlooking the main street
powerPositions.why: The map's dominant sightline, taken with a wall around you. This is the correct way to use the street.

powerPositions.name: The interior route parallel to the street
powerPositions.why: Moves you the length of the map without ever crossing the open middle.

enemySpots.name: The houses at either end
enemySpots.note: Snipers camping the end houses overlooking the main street are common. This is the signature Havana angle.

enemySpots.name: Building interiors along the street
enemySpots.note: The map has many buildings where combat and camping are both common.

enemySpots.name: The chokepoints
enemySpots.note: The map is full of them, and they're where people wait.

maps.trap: The main street. It's the direct route and it's covered end to end from the houses at both ends and from windows along the sides. Every death there is avoidable by taking an interior.

loadout.weaponWhy: 3-shot burst kill out to 58.4m — the longest reach available, and Havana's street is where reach pays.
loadout.perkWhy: The interior flank is the whole strategy, and it only works if you're off their minimap while you take it.

deeper: The map is the same shape as Crossfire from CoD4. If you know that map, you know this one's problem: a long central street nobody should walk down.
The map supports all weapon types well, so the enemy's loadouts will be varied — expect both an SMG rush and a sniper on the same life.
If you insist on a suppressor here, the M16 drops from a 3-shot kill at 58.4m to 26.4m. On this street that's the difference between winning and trading.
verified: Urban setting, described by Treyarch as a medium map
The same shape as Crossfire from Call of Duty 4
Snipers camping the end houses overlooking the main street are common
Many buildings, and a lot of chokepoints
Supports all weapon types well

maps.name: Grid
maps.identity: A Soviet communications facility — small buildings, hangars and generators across snow, with the comms grid at one end. In Team Deathmatch it's often a quiet map that rewards stealth.

sides.name: West end
sides.spawn: The western end of the facility.
sides.opening: Take the building on your side rather than racing for the truck in the centre. The centre is where everyone else is going.
sides.flank: Round the outside toward their building's blind side.
sides.pinch: The open ground beside the central truck. It's the busiest spot on the map and it's covered from both buildings.

sides.name: East end
sides.spawn: The eastern end, toward the trees and foliage.
sides.opening: Use the snowy foliage on the east to move without being seen, then take an angle on the centre.
sides.flank: Through the treeline and along the outside.
sides.pinch: Leaving the foliage for the open middle. You lose your concealment in one step.

powerPositions.name: One of the two buildings either side of the centre
powerPositions.why: Most of the fighting gravitates to the truck in the middle and these two buildings. Holding one means the traffic comes to you.

powerPositions.name: The snowy foliage on the east side
powerPositions.why: A large area of natural concealment, well suited to a patient game — especially with Ghost.

enemySpots.name: The two buildings flanking the centre
enemySpots.note: The map's main fighting positions.

enemySpots.name: In the eastern foliage
enemySpots.note: Ideal sniping ground, and Ghost users sit there because it works.

enemySpots.name: Around the central truck
enemySpots.note: The single busiest point on the map.

maps.trap: Rushing the truck in the centre. Fighting gravitates there naturally, which means both buildings already have angles on it. On a map that is quiet in TDM, being the one player sprinting into the middle makes you the only target.

loadout.weaponWhy: 3-shot kill to 45.7m suits the medium sightlines across the open snow without being useless indoors.
loadout.perkWhy: The wiki singles out Ghost users in the eastern foliage for a reason — this is a map where staying off the minimap and staying still actually wins games.

deeper: In Team Deathmatch this map is often quiet compared with the objective modes, which makes stealth approaches unusually effective.
One spawn has noticeably more cover, with fighting only occasionally reaching the corners — a good place to call in killstreaks safely.
There are two RC-XD ventilation shafts if you run one: a pipe in the trees to the east, and a building in the north to north-east.
verified: Small buildings, hangars and generators on a snowy landscape, with a power/comms grid at one end
Resembles a secret Soviet communications facility
Fighting gravitates to the truck in the centre and the two buildings either side
The east side has a large area of snowy foliage that is ideal for snipers, especially with Ghost
Often quiet in Team Deathmatch and open to stealth play
Two RC-XD ventilation shafts: a pipe in the eastern trees, and a building to the north/north-east

maps.name: Array
maps.identity: One of the larger maps, and more varied than it looks — a handful of routes that mix long-range fragging with close gun battles around a big open centre. Just about any weapon is usable here.

sides.name: Black Ops spawn
sides.spawn: The Black Ops end, off a huge open area.
sides.opening: A quick grenade at the doorway by the truck at the start of the round can get multiple kills — it's a major choke and people funnel there.
sides.flank: Toward centre array via the pallet and forklift, then the guard house.
sides.pinch: The stairs above the guardhouse. They're narrow, so it's a kill or be killed — and watch for claymores on them.

sides.name: Opposite spawn
sides.spawn: The far end, toward the crane.
sides.opening: The large crane gives a couple of levels and huge peeks down the side of the map. Take a look, take a kill, then move — good players work you out quickly.
sides.flank: The back tunnel in bottom array. It's underused and it gets you behind their lines fast.
sides.pinch: The open ground below the electrical tower. It's wide open and gets picked on constantly from centre array.

powerPositions.name: The legs of the electrical tower
powerPositions.why: You can jump onto them for excellent cover while keeping good peeks on the open ground — one of the best-value spots on the map, and it fixes the problem that the area below the tower is otherwise a shooting gallery.

powerPositions.name: Centre array, reached by climbing the boxes
powerPositions.why: Climbing up to centre array lets you avoid all the popular routes and chokes where you're most likely to be killed. Best ground, safest arrival.

enemySpots.name: Array Tower
enemySpots.note: The map's landmark and where people camp. The bunkers and trucks in the open area are the cover you use to get angles on them.

enemySpots.name: Under the wedge, by the hill
enemySpots.note: A specific camping spot. If you're on the hill, move fast and keep your eyes on it.

enemySpots.name: The crane and the satellite dish
enemySpots.note: Both climbable, both give long peeks — the dish looks down the electrical tower.

maps.trap: The open ground below the electrical tower. It's wide, it's overlooked from centre array, and it gets picked on by a lot of people. The rock area is the other one — a strong choke that's surrounded by spawns, so you can win a fight there and immediately have company.

loadout.weaponWhy: 58.4m of 3-shot kill range for the long routes — though Array genuinely supports anything, so bring what you shoot well.
loadout.perkWhy: Rotations are long, and the back tunnel only works as a flank if you aren't on their minimap while you take it.

deeper: The truck at the doorway won't blow up, so the back of it is genuine cover. Once it has been destroyed, the wreck becomes an elevated position with angles into both spawns.
The unfinished building has thin walls that will get you killed, but it offers a useful peek if you're just passing through.
You can jump onto a ledge in the ice cannon and be out of range of most grenades and bullets while prone.
Jumping out of the window onto the railing gives a spot that peeks the propane tank and the main entrance of Array Tower.
Claymores are common on the guardhouse stairs and in the rooms — check before you move through.
The pallet and forklift lead to the guard house; both are critical choke points for traffic.
Don't run a suppressor here. Cutting your full-damage range on a map this open is self-sabotage.
verified: One of the larger maps, offering a handful of routes for both long-range and close combat; just about any weapon is usable (ZigZack, IGN map recon)
A large open area with bunkers and trucks providing cover for angles on players camping in Array Tower (ZigZack)
A major choke at the truck by the doorway; a grenade at the start of the round can multi-kill; the truck won't blow up so its back is cover (ZigZack)
Once destroyed, the truck becomes an elevated position with angles into both spawns (ZigZack)
Players camp under the wedge near the hill (ZigZack)
A large crane offers a couple of levels and long peeks down the side of the map (ZigZack)
The satellite dish is climbable and peeks down the electrical tower; the unfinished building has thin walls but a useful peek (ZigZack)
The rock area is a strong choke point surrounded by spawns (ZigZack)
The stairs above the guardhouse are narrow and claymored; the pallet, forklift and guard house are critical traffic chokes (ZigZack)
A ledge in the ice cannon puts you out of range of most grenades and bullets when prone (ZigZack)
The area below the electrical tower is wide open and gets shot from centre array; jumping onto the tower's legs gives cover with good peeks (ZigZack)
Climbing the boxes to centre array avoids the popular routes and chokes (ZigZack)
A window-to-railing spot peeks the propane tank and the main entrance of Array Tower (ZigZack)
A back tunnel in bottom array is underused and gets you behind enemy lines quickly (ZigZack)
Centred on a large relay dish with surrounding buildings; large open areas make sniping prevalent (CoD Wiki)

maps.name: WMD
maps.identity: A fairly large snowed-in facility with real verticality — silos, a factory, catwalks, rafters and a middle house you can see most of the map from. Height is the whole game here.

sides.name: Spetsnaz (silos)
sides.spawn: The Spetsnaz side, below the silos.
sides.opening: Climb the elevated positions below the silos and use the distance. The sniper perch by the AC unit gives good cover and watches the middle.
sides.flank: Into the factory, which has three major entrances — from there you either watch players crossing the middle or watch for flankers.
sides.pinch: Crossing the middle in view of the silos. The elevated positions on that side exist precisely to punish it.

sides.name: Black Ops
sides.spawn: The Black Ops side.
sides.opening: Climb the ladder to the rafters — the most elevated position on the map. You can cover teammates from there and alternate between firing spots to keep the enemy guessing.
sides.flank: Cut through cat house to middle house, either jumping across or climbing from the ground up.
sides.pinch: The catwalk peek. It gives a wide view into the Black Ops spawn, which means it also looks straight back at you.

powerPositions.name: The rafters, above the Black Ops spawn
powerPositions.why: The most elevated position on the map, with enough spots to alternate your fire from so nobody pins down where you are.

powerPositions.name: The second level of middle house
powerPositions.why: A 360-degree view of most of the map. The ground floor is a death trap with four entrances; the level above it is the reason to go there at all.

enemySpots.name: The warehouse overlooking the silos
enemySpots.note: Explicitly a camper's haven. From its top there's a clear view of the whole silo area.

enemySpots.name: The sniper perch by the AC unit
enemySpots.note: Good cover watching the middle. Assume it's occupied before you cross.

enemySpots.name: The factory's three entrances and the catwalk
enemySpots.note: Both watch the middle crossings and the flank routes.

maps.trap: Playing middle house on the ground floor. It has four main entrances, which makes it a very risky area — you cannot watch them all, and people arrive from every side. The second level is what you actually came for; the ground floor is where you die.

loadout.weaponWhy: 3-shot kill to 45.7m with manageable recoil — the lanes are long enough to punish an SMG without demanding a full long-range build.
loadout.perkWhy: The flank routes through cat house and the factory only work if they can't see you take them.

deeper: The stairs give good cover against players rushing out of the Black Ops spawn, especially against the cat house windows.
Verticality is the point of this map: silos, sniper perch, factory, catwalk, rafters and middle house's upper level are all elevated. Before you cross anything, look up.
A freight train passes on the west-side railway at random times — noise cover that works both ways.
The catwalk is reached by ladder and sees a good portion of the map, but it is a known route rather than a hidden one.
verified: A fairly large map (ZigZack, IGN map recon)
Below the silos there are elevated positions to climb and use the distance from (ZigZack)

Cat house connects to middle house; you can jump across or climb from the ground (ZigZack)

A Nova 6 facility in the Soviet Union; a freight train passes on the west-side railway (CoD Wiki)

maps.name: Launch
maps.identity: Not actually a small map, though it plays like one because everybody forces the same few routes. The middle is split in two by railroad tracks and is deeply unstable — this is a team map, and solo heroics do not get through enemy lines.

sides.name: Spetsnaz
sides.spawn: The Spetsnaz side. The back area behind it is wide open with a handful of spawn points — which is exactly why air strikes land there.
sides.opening: Push up the left side toward the middle, but expect it: that's the most popular choke breaching this spawn, and it will be full of grenades and flashes.
sides.flank: Bottom rocket into the three-storey area, which takes you up to top rocket with one press of sprint.
sides.pinch: The left-side choke. If you get through the nades and flashes you reach the centre — plenty don't.

sides.name: Black Ops
sides.spawn: The Black Ops side. More confined, which funnels foot traffic into a single area.
sides.opening: Push out. Getting spawn trapped here is very hard to recover from, so the priority is not letting it start.
sides.flank: The mirrored bridge, or the identical three-storey route on this side of the rocket for long peeks on enemies spawning opposite.
sides.pinch: The back rooms of your own spawn — a popular spot for enemy equipment. Check for claymores and tactical insertions.

powerPositions.name: Top rocket, via the three-storey area
powerPositions.why: Both sides have an identical three-storey route from bottom rocket to top rocket that you clear with one press of sprint. The same jumps on the far side of the rocket give long-range peeks onto enemies spawning opposite.

powerPositions.name: The middle crossing that overlooks the centre
powerPositions.why: A major route into the Spetsnaz side, and it gets exceptional vision on anyone running straight through the middle.

enemySpots.name: Overlooking the middle
enemySpots.note: Most firefights start and end in the centre, and the routes across it are watched.

enemySpots.name: The back Black Ops spawn rooms
enemySpots.note: A popular area for equipment — claymores and tactical insertions rather than players.

enemySpots.name: The three-storey areas either side of the rocket
enemySpots.note: Both sides are identical, so whatever you're doing, they can do back.

maps.trap: The middle. It's split in two by the railroad tracks and it is almost impossible to watch every angle — most firefights and most deaths start and end there. Solo pushes through it are the specific thing this map punishes.

loadout.weaponWhy: 45.7m of 3-shot range handles the medium-long lanes without being useless inside the structures.
loadout.perkWhy: A lot of fights here are through structures and at ranges where flinch decides the trade.

deeper: The barriers in the middle are bulletproof — real cover, not decoration. Use them rather than sprinting between them.
Air strikes on the open back area of the Spetsnaz spawn are unusually effective because of the number of spawn points clustered there.
Getting spawn trapped in the Black Ops spawn is very difficult to recover from. If your team is being pinned, the answer is a coordinated push out, not individuals trying to break it.
The rocket launches around the halfway point and kills anyone beneath the engines — decide in advance where you'll be.
This map rewards playing with your team more than any other in the rotation.
verified: Not considered a small map, though most people feel like it is; plenty of routes exist but most players force the popular ones (ZigZack, IGN map recon)

The Black Ops spawn is more confined with concentrated foot traffic; its back rooms are a popular equipment spot — check for claymores and tactical insertions (ZigZack)
Being spawn trapped in the Black Ops spawn is very hard to recover from (ZigZack)

A mirrored bridge leads back to the Spetsnaz side; a middle route gets exceptional vision on people running through the middle (ZigZack)
Most firefights and deaths start and end in the middle (ZigZack)

maps.name: Villa
maps.identity: A large house on a clifftop with a big open courtyard at its centre. The villa overlooks the courtyard, which makes crossing the open middle the single worst habit you can have here.

sides.name: Lower end
sides.spawn: The lower ground below the villa.
sides.opening: Work up the sides using cover. Anyone crossing the open courtyard is being watched from the villa above.
sides.flank: Round the flanks past the pool area, staying behind the rock cover.
sides.pinch: The courtyard's open centre. Rock cover exists — use it, or the villa's overlook will find you.

sides.name: Villa end
sides.spawn: The villa side, above the courtyard.
sides.opening: Hold the overlook. You have the map's dominant position; giving it up to push down is how you lose it.
sides.flank: Down the side routes rather than straight across the courtyard.
sides.pinch: The stairs and entrances down from the villa. Enclosed and easy to hold from below.

powerPositions.name: The villa overlooking the courtyard
powerPositions.why: Explicitly the map's winning position — players find success picking off anyone who runs into the open below.

powerPositions.name: The flanking routes with cover
powerPositions.why: The wiki's own observation: players who flank the sides and use cover are much harder to hit than those crossing the open.

enemySpots.name: The villa's overlook
enemySpots.note: Assume it's occupied every time you consider crossing the courtyard.

enemySpots.name: Around the rock cover in the courtyard
enemySpots.note: The middle has cover, and people use it to hold rather than cross.

enemySpots.name: The cliff edges
enemySpots.note: The map's edges play like Cliffside — narrow and exposed.

maps.trap: Running into the open courtyard. It is the map's defining mistake: the villa overlooks it, players there make a living off exactly that, and anyone who takes the covered flanks instead is far harder to kill.

loadout.weaponWhy: 3-shot kill to 45.7m covers the courtyard's sightlines while staying usable in the house.
loadout.perkWhy: The interiors are enclosed and multi-level, so footsteps carry more information than sightlines do.

deeper: The courtyard is a large open space with rock cover, like Courtyard. Cover is there — the mistake is sprinting past it, not being in the middle.
The map edges resemble Cliffside: narrow, exposed, and a long way down.
Grenades roll downhill. From the villa that's in your favour; from below it isn't.
verified: A large house setting, situated atop a cliff
Map edges have similar qualities to Cliffside
The centre features a large open space with rock cover, similar to Courtyard
The villa overlooks the courtyard and certain objectives
Players find success picking off enemies who run into the open; those who flank the sides and use cover are harder to hit
There is a pool area

maps.name: Crisis
maps.identity: A hidden Cuban missile facility with a beach on one flank — intense indoor and outdoor fighting. Similar ground to Jungle, but with more buildings and open sand.

sides.name: Beach end
sides.spawn: Toward the beach and the landing craft.
sides.opening: Move inland toward the main building. The beach is open and the hill above it is where the snipers sit.
sides.flank: Through the buildings rather than along the sand.
sides.pinch: The open sand. It's overlooked from the hill, and there's very little on it to hide behind.

sides.name: Facility end
sides.spawn: The facility side, inland.
sides.opening: Straight for the second floor of the main building — it's one of the three places this map is actually fought over.
sides.flank: Round via the rocket-head building into their approach.
sides.pinch: The doorways of the main building. Contested constantly and covered from inside.

powerPositions.name: The second floor of the main building
powerPositions.why: One of the three areas where battles are common on this map, and the most useful of them in TDM.

powerPositions.name: The building in front of the main building, with the rocket-head inside
powerPositions.why: The other central contested space — holding it means controlling the approach to the main building.

enemySpots.name: The sniper mountain at the top of the hill
enemySpots.note: Exactly what it sounds like, and it covers the open ground. Check it before you cross the beach.

enemySpots.name: The second floor of the main building
enemySpots.note: The map's busiest interior.

enemySpots.name: The rocket-head building
enemySpots.note: The third of the three common battle areas.

maps.trap: Crossing the open beach. It's wide, bright, and overlooked from the hill where the snipers sit. It looks like a free flank because it's empty — it's empty because it doesn't work.

loadout.weaponWhy: 39.4m of 3-shot range and a 128ms kill — enough reach for the outdoor half, fast enough for the interiors.
loadout.perkWhy: The interior route between the contested buildings is the good one, and it needs you off their minimap.

deeper: Three areas carry almost all the fighting: the second floor of the main building, the sniper mountain on the hill, and the rocket-head building. If you know where those are, you know where everyone is.
The map runs indoor and outdoor games at once — pick which one you're playing before you spawn and take the loadout for it.
Smoke genuinely works if your team has to cross the open half.
verified: A hidden missile facility in Cuba, with intense indoor and outdoor battles
Similar environment to Jungle but with more buildings and a beach
Landing craft on the beach; likely the Bay of Pigs
The three areas where battles are common: the second floor of the main building, the sniper mountain at the top of the hill, and the building in front of the main building with the rocket-head inside

maps.name: Cracked
maps.identity: Bombed-out urban blocks modelled on Hue City, with one or two buildings in the middle sitting on the cracked ground the map is named after. Multi-level and full of angles.

sides.name: North-west end
sides.spawn: The north-western blocks.
sides.opening: Into the buildings and up a level, then take an angle onto the middle rather than walking into it.
sides.flank: Through the interiors parallel to the centre into their blocks.
sides.pinch: The crossings into the central buildings. Rubble gives partial cover, which is worse than none — it feels safe while you're visible.

sides.name: South-east end
sides.spawn: The south-eastern blocks, near the boats.
sides.opening: Up into your buildings first, then work toward the centre from height.
sides.flank: Along the back of the buildings into their half.
sides.pinch: The gaps between blocks. Short, and overlooked from upper floors on both sides.

powerPositions.name: An upper floor overlooking the centre
powerPositions.why: The central buildings are what the map is fought over, and you want to be looking down into them rather than standing in them.

powerPositions.name: The interior route parallel to the middle
powerPositions.why: Moves you across the map without crossing the contested centre.

enemySpots.name: Upper floors and windows
enemySpots.note: This is a look-up map. Most deaths come from above ground level.

enemySpots.name: The central buildings
enemySpots.note: The middle of the map and the objective location in most modes — always contested.

enemySpots.name: Stairwells
enemySpots.note: Watching the only way up.

maps.trap: Fighting at ground level in the middle. The central buildings are overlooked from upper floors all around, and the cracked rubble that looks like cover only hides you from other people on the ground.

loadout.weaponWhy: Fast and accurate, with 39.4m of 3-shot range covering both the street lengths and the interior fights.
loadout.perkWhy: Multi-level buildings mean enemies are constantly above or below you, and footsteps are the difference between clearing a floor and dying on the stairs.

deeper: Decide whether you're going up or holding the ground floor when you enter a building. Doing both gets you caught on the stairs.
The map is the basis for the campaign mission The Defector, and resembles Hue City from Full Metal Jacket — if the layout feels familiar, that's why.
A claymore on the stairwell behind you buys the freedom to watch one direction properly.
verified: Urban map, the basis for the campaign mission The Defector
One or two buildings in the middle surrounded by cracked terrain — the map's namesake and the central objective location
Bears a strong resemblance to Hue City from Full Metal Jacket
Asian-style boats sit behind the SOG spawn

spawnSystem.how: The game respawns you in the safest spot that isn't blocked by an enemy. It constantly re-reads where both teams are standing, so the spawn map moves as you do.
triggers: Pushing deep into the enemy's back half
Your team spreading too thin across the map
Wiping the whole enemy side at once, leaving nowhere safe on their end
Physically standing on or near their spawn points
Holding a power position that reaches into their territory
tells: A teammate appears from the direction the enemy came from
Kills start arriving from a new direction
A part of the map that was busy goes silent — they've been moved
spawnSystem.source: General Call of Duty spawn-flip mechanics (MitchCactus), corroborated for BO1 on Nuketown by a 2011 map guide describing enemies respawning behind your lines once your team pushes past the bus.
